I am 71 years old. I never went to school. My father put the hoe in my hand when I was sixteen and I have farmed these same 2 mu in Quzhou ever since. My wife and I do all the work ourselves. We have a well for water but pumping costs diesel, so I count every time I turn on the pump.

For winter wheat, I plant the improved seed that everyone in the village gets from the shop. I sow about 25 jin per mu. I always buy one big bag of urea — that is 100 jin — for the 2 mu, and I spread half before sowing and half in March when the wheat turns green. I also buy one bag of compound fertilizer, 100 jin for the 2 mu, and put it all down before sowing. That is 50 jin of each per mu. I irrigate three times: once after sowing if the soil is dry, once in March, and once in May when the grain is filling. I spray twice — herbicide right after sowing and insecticide in spring when the bugs come. After the maize comes off in October, I hire the rotary tiller to soften the ground for wheat.

For summer maize, I plant hybrid seed, about 4 jin per mu, dropped by the machine right after wheat harvest in June. I buy another 100 jin bag of urea for the 2 mu and put it down when the maize is knee-high. I do not buy new compound for maize; the wheat ground still has some food in it. I irrigate twice if the rain does not come — once when the stalks are tall and once when the cobs need filling. I spray once for weeds and once for the bugs that eat the leaves. I do not till for maize; there is no time after wheat harvest, so the planter goes straight into the wheat stubble.

I expect my wheat to give me about 900 jin per mu and my maize about 1000 jin per mu. Last year was about the same. I do not change what works. My nephew tried to save money on fertilizer two years ago and his wheat was thin like grass. I would rather spend the extra yuan on one more bag of urea than risk losing the harvest. This land is all my wife and I have.
